items.title: Make WorkerService.appendLog an atomic SQL append instead of a read-modify-write of the whole job row
items.body:
## Problem
`bridge/apps/backend/src/worker/worker.service.ts:334-340` implements `appendLog` as `findOwned` -> `job.logs += chunk` -> `jobRepository.save(job)`. Two consequences:

1. **Lost updates / status clobbering.** `save(job)` writes the whole entity as loaded. While a log POST is in flight, `cancel()` (lines 223-253), `updateStatus()` (265-312) or `failLostJobs()` (125-146) can change the same row; whichever save lands last wins. A log chunk landing just after a `cancelled`/`failed` transition can write back the stale `status`, `cancelRequestedAt` or `finishedAt`.
2. **O(n^2) write volume.** The worker flushes every ~1.5s (`worker/src/index.ts:33,84-93`), and every flush reads and rewrites the entire, ever-growing `logs` text. A chatty job with a 1 MiB output tail rewrites hundreds of KiB per flush.

The comment at `worker/src/index.ts:77-80` shows the client already works around ordering problems on its side, but the server-side append is not atomic.

## Proposed change
Replace the body with a single statement, e.g. `this.jobRepository.query('UPDATE jobs SET logs = logs || $1, "updatedAt" = now() WHERE id = $2 AND "userId" = $3', [chunk, id, userId])` (or a QueryBuilder `update` with `logs: () => 'logs || :chunk'`), keeping the ownership check (404 when no row is affected). Optionally cap the stored log at a fixed size (e.g. keep the last N KiB) in the same SQL. Do not touch the `status`/`finishedAt` columns.

## Acceptance criteria
- `appendLog` no longer loads and saves the whole `Job` entity.
- Appending to another user's job id still throws `NotFoundException`.
- A unit test shows two sequential appends concatenate in order, and that an append does not change `status`, `finishedAt` or `cancelRequestedAt`.
- Existing worker service tests and the e2e suite still pass (`npm test -w backend`).
- The change is under ~100 lines.

items.title: Add a deadline to claudeChat so a hung claude CLI cannot freeze the worker on a chat turn
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/chatRunners/claudeChat.ts:34` calls `runClaude(turnDir, prompt, claudeModel, () => {}, proxyUrl)` and passes no `timeoutMs` (7th parameter of `runClaude`, `worker/src/modelRunners/claudeRunner.ts:30`), no `signal`, and no `claudeToken`. With `timeoutMs` undefined, the timer at `claudeRunner.ts:72-79` is never created, so a stuck `claude -p` process never exits. `processChatTurn` is awaited inline by the single-threaded poll loop (`worker/src/index.ts:283-284`), so one hung chat turn stops all job and chat polling and the heartbeat, and the worker shows as down on the Worker page. Jobs already pass `config.jobTimeoutSec * 1000` (`index.ts:157`); chat turns do not.

Also, `claudeChat.ts:40` returns `result.output.trim()` without checking it is non-empty, so a CLI that exits 0 with no output completes the chat message with an empty reply.

## Proposed change
- Add a `timeoutMs` parameter to `claudeChat` (default e.g. 5 minutes, or a new `CHAT_TURN_TIMEOUT_SEC` value in `worker/src/config.ts` next to the job timeout) and pass it to `runClaude`. Thread it from `processChatTurn` in `index.ts:233`.
- Throw a clear error (`claude returned an empty reply`) when the trimmed output is empty, so `client.fail` reports it instead of an empty success.

## Acceptance criteria
- `claudeChat` passes a positive `timeoutMs` to `runClaude`.
- A test with a fake `claude` binary that sleeps (see how `claudeRunner.test.ts` stubs the CLI, if present) shows the turn fails with the 'timed out' message and the temp dir is removed.
- A test shows an exit-0, empty-output run rejects instead of returning an empty string.
- `cd worker && npm test` and `npm run lint` pass.

items.title: Validate the id argument of the get_job chat tool instead of building /worker/jobs/NaN
items.body:
## Problem
`worker/src/chatTools.ts:136` does `api(`/worker/jobs/${Number(args.id)}`)` with no check on what the model supplied. The id comes from LLM tool-call arguments, so a missing, string or fractional id becomes `/worker/jobs/NaN` or `/worker/jobs/1.5`. Bridge answers with a 400 from `ParseIntPipe`. The model then sees an opaque `Tool get_job failed: bridge answered 400: ...` message, which wastes a tool round-trip and invites it to guess. `create_job` in the same file already validates with `Number.isInteger` (lines 153-158), so the two tools are inconsistent. `worker/src/chatTools.test.ts:78-86` covers only the happy path of `get_job`; no test passes a bad id.

## Proposed change
In the `get_job` case, parse `const id = Number(args.id)` and return `'get_job needs an integer id.'` (without calling fetch) when `!Number.isInteger(id) || id < 1`. Add tests for `{}`, `{ id: 'abc' }` and `{ id: 1.5 }` asserting the message and that no request was made (reuse the `stubBridge` calls array).

## Acceptance criteria
- `get_job` with a missing, non-numeric, fractional or non-positive id returns a readable message and makes zero fetch calls.
- `get_job` with `{ id: 9 }` behaves exactly as before.
- New tests in `worker/src/chatTools.test.ts` pass with `cd worker && npm test`; lint passes.

items.title: Log a warning when encryptedColumn.from cannot decrypt a value, and test tampered/rotated-key cases
items.body:
## Problem
`bridge/apps/backend/src/crypto/encrypted-column.transformer.ts:70-91` swallows every decryption failure (`catch { return value; }`) and silently hands the raw `v1:iv:tag:ciphertext` string back to callers. The comment calls this the right failure mode, but nothing is logged. A missing or wrongly rotated `CREDENTIALS_ENC_KEY`, or a corrupted row, therefore shows up only as a downstream failure: the `claude` CLI is given the ciphertext string as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` (`worker/src/modelRunners/claudeRunner.ts:53`), or a VPN panel request is sent the ciphertext as its API token. In both cases the admin sees an auth error from a third party, not 'key misconfigured'. Worse, `Secret.value` is revealed to the user through `SecretsService.revealValue` (`secrets/secrets.service.ts:89-97`), so the ciphertext would be shown as if it were the secret.

Test gaps: `encrypted-column.transformer.spec.ts:51-55` covers only the missing-key fallback. There is no test for a tampered auth tag or ciphertext (GCM integrity), a wrong-length key, or a legacy plaintext value that happens to contain exactly three colons (the `parts.length !== 4` check at line 66 then routes it into the decrypt path).

## Proposed change
- Add a Nest `Logger` (or `console.warn`, matching the file's no-DI style) call in the catch block that logs the key id and the error message, never the value. De-duplicate per key id so it does not spam on every row read.
- Add spec cases: tampered ciphertext returns the raw value; tampered auth tag returns the raw value; a plaintext legacy value like `a:b:c:d` round-trips unchanged; a wrong-length key makes `to()` throw the documented message.

## Acceptance criteria
- A failed decryption emits exactly one warning per key id that names the key id and the env var, and never contains the stored value.
- Behavior is unchanged: `from` still returns the raw stored value on failure.
- The four new spec cases pass with `npm test -w backend`.
- The change is under ~80 lines.
